Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{2} & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -\frac{3}{2} & 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=1,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=1+1+2=4.
$$
